title: Officers cleared in death of a 'gentle giant'
article: The Special Investigations Unit (SIU) has cleared two Toronto police officers of any wrongdoing in the Aug. 1, 2011 death of Charles McGillivary.
The case, in which McGillivary collapsed and died on Bloor Street near Christie Street while being arrested by police, sparked outrage in the community.

The 46-year-old McGillivary was disabled and had been unable to speak following a childhood accident. He was arrested when police mistook him for another man who was being sought for breach of bail conditions.
A vigil was held for the victim, known as a gentle giant by those who knew him, following his death.
According to the SIU investigation, the officers called out "Raymond" - the name of the suspect they were seeking - and pursued McGillivary, believing him to be the man they were seeking.
Because McGillivary was unable to communicate with the officers and resisted being handcuffed, one of the officers knocked him down using a leg sweep, according to evidence presented to the SIU.

The victim fell into medical distress after being handcuffed and efforts by the officers to resuscitate him were unsuccessful. An ambulance brought him to Toronto Western Hospital, where he was pronounced dead.
McGillivary had an underlying heart condition, which is believed to have led to his death.

SIU director Ian Scott said the officers "held an honest and reasonable but ultimately mistaken belief that the person they apprehended with respect to this incident was the man they were looking for."
He added the outcome of the incident could not have been foreseen and that eyewitness and video evidence shows the officers did not use undue force given the circumstances.
The officers were cleared of any wrongdoing in the case.
